topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture structure, learning outcomes, and the multi-step progression model of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling and growth suppressor evasion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how oncogenic mutations in surface receptors and intracellular cascades, such as Wnt/beta-catenin, RTK, and TGF-beta pathways, confer self-sufficiency in growth signals and insensitivity to anti-growth signals.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells fail to withdraw from the cell cycle and differentiate into mature functional states across hematological and epithelial malignancies.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how tumor cells avoid programmed cell death through the dysregulation of p53, MDM2, and Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress surveillance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms of telomere biology, cellular senescence, telomerase reactivation, and p53-mediated genome surveillance that regulate cellular lifespan.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the metabolic rewiring of cancer cells, including the Warburg effect, tissue-of-origin metabolic profiles, and Krebs cycle mutations producing oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic focuses on the angiogenic switch and blood vessel recruitment necessary to supply oxygen and nutrients to growing tumors.

topics.label: Invasion, circulation, and metastatic progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the multi-step metastatic cascade, circulating tumor cell monitoring, seed-and-soil interactions, and the genomic features underlying secondary site colonization.

topics.label: Concluding summary and outlook
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic synthesizes the lecture themes and provides concluding remarks regarding the cancer hallmarks literature.
